title: Delirium Superimposed on Dementia in Nursing Homes: A Prospective Study on Occurrence, Prognosis, and Care Processes
summary:
DeliDem-NH is a prospective, multicentre observational study conducted in nursing homes. The study aims to systematically assess the prevalence and incidence of potential delirium in residents with dementia, identify associated risk factors, and examine course, prognosis, and cognitive, functional, and physical outcomes.

Participants without delirium at baseline (Cohort B) will be followed weekly for six months. Potential delirium will be assessed using validated screening instruments; in cases of suspected delirium, symptom severity and subtype will be documented. Cognitive and functional parameters as well as physical activity will be measured at baseline; cognitive and functional assessments will be repeated at six months and repeated three months later.  Nursing and medical care processes initiated in response to potential delirium will be described once.

The study addresses a critical gap in epidemiological data on delirium in residents with moderate to severe dementia in long-term care facilities and provides a foundation for the development of targeted prevention and care interventions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- documented diagnosis of dementia
- Dementia Screening Scale (score > 2)
- informed consent from the legal representative
Exclusion criteria:
- aphasia
- terminal condition, deafness
- severe hearing impairment
- inability to communicate in the German language
